obligations.note: The new error-path log call in deliver_statement puts the payee's unmasked account_number (an NPI field in payments.npi_fields) into the log message via an f-string. Field-level masking in AppLog cannot redact it there, so NPI reaches the application log on the error path.

The diff changes only the log line in the IntegrationError handler of deliver_statement. Every _audit call in service.py is unchanged, and the success path still records deliver_statement with actor, action, target and time.
The register has no exception for LOG-1 on payments.service or payments.logging. EXC-0167 covers mortgage.logging and masked last-4 only, so the LOG-1 deviation is not excepted.
Ticket CHG-26050 is standard and was approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) on 2026-10-21, before review. Its components (payments.service) cover the only touched path, service.py.
Sofia Santos approved the code_review. She holds change_approver for payments and is a different person from the author, Linh Nguyen.
The code_review approval names the head commit fd8db494, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims ci-runner-04 ran the head commit at 2026-10-22T15:36Z, exactly the commit time. The JUnit report, however, has hostname dev-laptop-7.local and timestamp 2026-10-23T13:51-07:00, so the report's provenance from the change's own CI run cannot be established.
The only touched path, service.py, maps to payments.service, which is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected path (controls data, control tests, ci) is changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The change is not an emergency (emergency=false, ticket type standard), so no post-implementation review is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers service.py. The entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files, none of which changed, so no evidence lapses.

summary: PR-1537 changes the statement-delivery failure log to interpolate the payee's raw account number into the log message. That sends unmasked NPI to application logs on the error path, violating LOG-1, and no approved exception covers it. The process records (ticket, independent approval, approval on head) are in order. The CI evidence is inconsistent: the JUnit report appears to come from a local machine, not ci-runner-04. The LOG-1 violation alone requires rejection.
